verdictStoreContractProposed.table: parcel_gate_verdict (county_fips, rail_key, verdict[pass|refuse|excluded], unaccounted_count, evaluated_at, run_id) PRIMARY KEY (county_fips, rail_key)
verdictStoreContractProposed.rationale: documented verbatim as a code comment at the top of parcelGateVerdictRead.ts so PARCEL-B-GATE-SCHED's implementer sees it immediately on opening the file this card's PR touches. If that card's own close proposes a different shape, this card's own instruction is explicit: stop and report, never reconcile silently.
verdictStoreContractProposed.readerTreatsIdentically: a missing row and a query error (including relation-does-not-exist, i.e. the scheduler has not created the table yet) both resolve to null -- the allowlist's fail-closed behavior does not need its own try/catch.

designDecisions: Companion rails need no rail-metadata lookup: the reader unconditionally queries parcel_record_companion_row alongside parcel_record_cell for every rail; a scalar rail's companion rows are simply always empty. Avoids duplicating hauska-engine's PARCEL_RECORD_RAIL_META, which is not published for cross-repo consumption.

unaccounted maps to a REFUSAL (code 'unaccounted'), never a served word, matching this repo's own *FactRead.ts house convention (an unexamined fact is a refused facet) and _decisions/2026-09-01_serve_path_never_emits_pipeline_state.md's no-fifth-state rule -- verified this rule's text directly against verdictLayerServe.ts's own LAYER_ABSENCE_VERDICTS enum, which DOES carry 'unmeasured' as a member; that enum is the pattern the ruling calls a leak, not a precedent to extend for parcel_record's own reader.

Structurally read-only enforced via `SET default_transaction_read_only = on` on every pooled connection's 'connect' event, not just by omitting write code -- FACTORY_DATABASE_URL (verified via gcloud secrets list, no read-only variant exists) retains its own write grants at the credential level; a dedicated SELECT-only DB role would be stronger defense-in-depth and is named as leave_behind, not built here.

The allowlist's slate check runs FIRST, synchronously, in memory, before any verdict-store query -- caught and fixed during design: an earlier draft queried the verdict store unconditionally, which would have added a real DB round trip to brokerageNodeFacets.ts's zero-AI zero-live-compute anonymous public hot path on every request, for a pair that can only ever resolve to legacy today. Proven by a spy-based test (the store must never even be called for an unslated pair, not just 'fails gracefully if called').

Chose ONE real integration point (wells, brokerageNodeFacets.ts) over wiring all five slate-1 candidate rails or building a generic dispatcher -- proves the mechanism is live (not the dormant-code defect the step-5 review found for the publish gate) without overclaiming per-rail wire adapters that are honestly PARCEL-B-SLATE1's scope. The parallel wells call site in propertyExplorer.ts is intentionally left unwired, named as leave_behind.

The wrapper's unreachable 'record' branch (empty slate today) returns a typed refusal naming exactly why (adapter not built, PARCEL-B-SLATE1's job) rather than throwing or fabricating a plausible-looking present/absent shape -- required a new WellFactRefusal code ('parcel-record-adapter-not-built') rather than reusing an existing code with a misleading name.
